bills.title: Homeowners Premium Tax Reduction Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9978 directly implicates the Internal Revenue Service and Treasury's Office of Tax Policy because it would create or expand a tax deduction or credit reducing federal revenue from homeowner insurance premiums. Treasury must assess the static and dynamic revenue cost, design anti-abuse rules, and determine IRS administrative capacity to verify eligible premium payments at scale.

bills.title: A bill to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to improve the process for providing refunds to taxpayers.
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 5142 directly implicates IRS authority under Title 26 and falls within the jurisdiction of the Office of Tax Policy, which would need to assess any statutory changes to refund procedures, timelines, or interest accrual rules. Treasury's implementation risk centers on IRS operational capacity and systems readiness to execute revised refund processes, as well as potential budgetary exposure if accelerated refund timelines increase improper payment vulnerability.

bills.title: A bill to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to eliminate installment agreement fees for certain individuals.
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 5144 directly affects IRS revenue collection operations under Treasury's tax administration authority, as installment agreement user fees are set and collected pursuant to IRC Section 6159 and related Office of Management and Budget cost-recovery guidance. Eliminating fees for certain taxpayers would reduce IRS offsetting collections, requiring Treasury and IRS to assess the fiscal impact and determine whether appropriated funds or restructured fee schedules for other filers must compensate for the lost revenue.

bills.title: ABLE MATCH (Making Able a Tool to Combat Hardship) Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9801 directly implicates Treasury's Office of Tax Policy and IRS because ABLE accounts are tax-advantaged savings vehicles governed under IRC Section 529A, making Treasury the primary regulatory authority for any statutory changes to contribution rules or matching incentives. The implementation risk centers on IRS's responsibility to issue guidance, update Form 5498-QA reporting requirements, and coordinate with states administering ABLE programs to operationalize any new federal matching structure.

bills.title: A bill to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to impose limitations on high-income taxpayers with large retirement account balances.
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 5040 directly implicates IRS and Treasury's Office of Tax Policy, as it would amend the Internal Revenue Code to cap retirement account balances for high-income individuals and trigger required distributions or contribution prohibitions above set thresholds. Treasury faces significant implementation risk because the proposal would require new IRS guidance, reporting infrastructure, and enforcement mechanisms to identify and act on out-of-compliance balances across multiple account types.

bills.title: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to impose limitations on high-income taxpayers with large retirement account balances.
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9813 directly implicates IRS and Treasury's Office of Tax Policy, as it would amend the Internal Revenue Code to cap tax-advantaged retirement balances for high-income earners. Treasury faces significant implementation risk around required minimum distribution rule changes, valuation methodologies for non-publicly traded assets, and IRS enforcement capacity to monitor account thresholds at scale.

bills.title: Putting Patients First by Strengthening Provider Accountability in FECA Act
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
bills.nexus: H.R. 8823 amends the Federal Employees' Compensation Act (FECA), which is administered by the Department of Labor, not Treasury, and its provider accountability provisions do not implicate Treasury's tax, fiscal, or financial regulatory authorities. Treasury should monitor for any appropriations or payment integrity provisions that could affect federal workers' compensation outlays scored against the federal budget, but absent a known nexus, this bill presents no direct Treasury equities at this stage.

bills.title: Tariff Refund Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus:
Without a known nexus provided, here is a placeholder brief based on the bill title alone:

H.R. 9768 would require refunds of collected tariff revenues, directly implicating U.S. Customs and Border Protection's revenue collections and Treasury's authority over the Customs Revenue Function under 19 U.S.C. The implementation risk centers on the Office of Tax Policy and CBP coordinating refund mechanisms, potential revenue scoring impacts on the federal budget, and administrative burden on the customs drawback system.

bills.title: Disclosure of Tax Havens and Offshoring Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9761 would require public country-by-country reporting of corporate tax and financial data, directly implicating IRS authority under the Internal Revenue Code and Treasury's tax policy office (Office of Tax Policy). Treasury's implementation risk centers on reconciling new public disclosure mandates with existing taxpayer confidentiality rules under IRC Section 6103 and coordinating with SEC rulemaking given the bill's referral to Financial Services.

bills.title: HONOR Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: Without a confirmed nexus on file, I can flag the referral angle: Ways and Means jurisdiction signals the bill likely touches tax expenditures, tariffs, or trade, all areas where Treasury's Office of Tax Policy or the Office of Tariff Affairs and Trade Agreements would have equities. Treasury should monitor for any revenue scoring implications or regulatory implementation duties that could fall to IRS or USTR coordination.

bills.title: A resolution celebrating the historic significance of the 2026 Federation Internationale de Football Association (FIFA) World Cup and welcoming the international community to North America for the first tournament hosted by 3 nations.
bills.status: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4117; text: CR S4109)
bills.nexus: S.Res. 805 is a purely celebratory Senate resolution with no legislative text creating new law, appropriations, or regulatory authority, meaning it touches no Treasury office or statutory mandate. Treasury has no implementation role and faces no fiscal or regulatory risk from this measure.

bills.title: HONOR Act
bills.nexus: S. 327, the HONOR Act, is held at the desk with no confirmed nexus to Treasury's statutory authorities or program offices yet identified. Until referral or legislative text confirms a hook to tax administration, sanctions, AML/CFT, debt management, or financial stability, Treasury has no clear implementation obligation or regulatory risk to flag.
